entry.evidence: Several open questions remain, however: (1) the timing the uplift of the Bogda Mountains to the southeast of the basin is unclear.

sequences.source_document: Zhou et al. 2022, Ore Geology Reviews 146, 104922 (published PDF and XML abstract/captions)

steps.action: Review published reconstructions of Jurassic paleoclimate (humid Early Jurassic to arid Late Jurassic) and of provenance shifts among the North Tianshan, Central Tianshan and Bogda ranges.
steps.quote: suggest that the local climate was generally warm and humid in the Early Jurassic

steps.action: Pose open questions: the timing of Bogda uplift and the understudied role of the Kelameili and Zaire ranges as sources; note that a random-forest heavy-mineral result needs independent verification.
steps.quote: Several open questions remain, however: (1) the timing the uplift of the Bogda Mountains to the southeast of the basin is unclear.

steps.action: Design a multi-proxy outcrop study: sample eight sections covering the Lower, Middle and Upper Jurassic, using geochemical discrimination diagrams as an independent constraint.
steps.quote: Hence, we systematically sample eight sections

steps.action: Collect 21 sandstone samples; describe thin sections under optical microscope and SEM; measure major elements by XRF and trace elements and REE by ICP-MS (Tables 2-4).
steps.quote: 21 Jurassic sandstone samples from the southern margin of the Junggar Basin were collected for geochemical testing and analysis

steps.action: Assess XRF accuracy with duplicate samples and standard samples in each batch (Methods).
steps.quote: Three duplicate samples and two standard samples were used per batch for accuracy assessment.

steps.action: Separate and count heavy minerals in 20 samples; measure whole-rock and clay mineralogy by XRD; count detrital Q-F-L in thin sections (Tables 5-9).
steps.quote: Whole-rock and clay mineralogy were assessed using a polycrystalline D8A X-ray diffractometer (XRD)

steps.action: Compute CIA, with McLennan's carbonate-CaO correction, and read it against published thresholds as indicating weak weathering, an arid climate and slightly increasing drought upward.
steps.quote: The CIA value of Jurassic sandstone samples in the study area is 54.38–69.95, with an average value of 61.84

steps.action: Check the climate trend with clay mineral assemblages (kaolinite versus illite and chlorite) and report agreement with the CIA and element results.
steps.quote: The paleoclimate characteristics reflected by the change of clay mineral content are consistent with the analysis results of major and trace elements

steps.action: Infer provenance direction from the mapped distribution of quartz and lithic contents and from compositional maturity: southeast for the Lower Jurassic, northeast for the Upper Jurassic.
steps.quote: It is speculated that the provenance is mainly from the southeast

steps.action: Map the ZTR index of heavy minerals and compare its gradient with the clastic-component gradients.
steps.quote: This further proves that the Lower Jurassic provenance is mainly from the southeast

steps.action: Compare heavy-mineral assemblages (own samples plus data cited from Wan et al. 2009, Fang et al. 2006 and Lin et al. 2013) with the parent-rock assemblages of candidate source ranges tabulated after Zhou 2019, assigning sources by section and epoch.
steps.quote: the heavy mineral composition is similar to that of Zaire Mountain and Bogda Mountain (Table 11)

steps.action: Infer the tectonic setting of the source areas from major-element ratios against Bhatia's (1983) averages and from six oxide discrimination diagrams.
steps.quote: In the discrimination diagram of tectonic setting by oxide (Fig. 12), the sandstones in the study area mostly fall in the active continental margin.

steps.action: Re-assess the tectonic setting with trace-element ternary diagrams (Th-Co-Zr/10, Th-Sc-Zr/10, La-Sc-Th), which point mainly to continental island arc.
steps.quote: the Jurassic was mainly in continental island arc environment overall

steps.action: Compare REE parameters with Bhatia's setting ranges (Table 13) and REE trends with the major-element trends, reporting consistency with the oxide diagrams.
steps.quote: most of the samples in this study better match the characteristics of rare earth elements in the background of continental island arc.

steps.action: Apply Dickinson and Crook QFL/QFR detrital-mode diagrams to the Lower Jurassic samples as a petrographic check on the tectonic setting.
steps.quote: most of tectonic features of the provenance areas have the recycled-orogenic source

steps.action: Infer source-rock composition from K2O/Al2O3, Al2O3/TiO2 and trace-element ratios (La/Sc, Th/Sc, Cr/Th, Co/Th) against published thresholds, and from classification diagrams (Figs 16-17): felsic upper-crustal sources.
steps.quote: reflects that the provenance rocks in the study area are mainly felsic rocks in the upper crust.

steps.action: Check the (Fe2O3+MgO)-Na2O-K2O classification with the K-Rb diagram and further element diagrams, reporting agreement.
steps.quote: This is consistent with the conclusion of (Fe2O3total + MgO)-Na2O-K2O diagram.

steps.action: Keep three conclusions: an arid Jurassic climate drying upward; continental-island-arc and active-margin source settings with felsic upper-crustal source rocks; and source ranges by epoch.
steps.quote: Major and minor element discrimination and REE patterns indicate that the material was sourced from continental island arc and active continental margin environments

tree.answer: Composition and provenance of Jurassic sandstones on the southern Junggar margin, as a record of past climate, tectonic setting and source
No; climate, setting and source are read from geochemical and mineral traces through empirical thresholds and diagrams
Reconstruct paleoclimate, source tectonic setting, source rocks and source ranges
Candidate source ranges (Table 11) and setting classes on the discrimination diagrams; not posed as rivals with distinct tests
Only implicitly, through diagram fields and assemblage matches; no prediction is stated as decisive
Conditions found: outcrop strata sampled across eight sections and three epochs
Partly; multiple proxies are reported as mostly consistent, but the diagrams disagree on the setting (active margin versus island arc)
Claims kept as the best reconstruction

end.claim: Jurassic sandstones of the southern Junggar margin derive mainly from felsic upper-crustal sources in continental-island-arc and active-continental-margin settings, under an arid climate that dried upward, with source ranges shifting between the Lower and Upper Jurassic.

decisive_move.sentence: Projecting the major-element, trace-element and REE data onto published tectonic-setting discrimination diagrams produces the headline setting and source-rock claims; without these inferences there is no claim.

gates.evidence: Sampling was designed to cover sections and epochs, not directed by a stated hypothesis (p. 3-4). The claims meet only consistency checks among proxies (p. 9, 13, 19, 20) and could have failed only in the sense that proxies might disagree; where they do disagree (oxide diagrams point to active margin, trace-element diagrams to island arc), the claim merges both. No hypothesis, threshold or analysis is reported as fixed before the data.

novelty_claims.quote: Geochemical discrimination diagrams ... have not yet been applied in Jurassic sandstones on the southern margin.

limits: The XML text supplied contains only the abstract and captions, so body text is cited by PDF page. No review file was supplied, although the acknowledgements thank editors and anonymous reviewers. Internal inconsistencies the document does not resolve: (1) CIA (50-65) is read as arid for the whole Jurassic, while clay minerals are read as hot and humid for the Lower Jurassic, and the conclusion merges both as an 'arid paleoclimate' that was 'relatively humid' in the Early-Middle Jurassic (p. 9, 22-23). (2) The average K2O/Al2O3 values for the Lower and Upper Jurassic are given as 28.31 and 27.61, the same numbers as the Al2O3/TiO2 averages (p. 19-20), which looks like a copying error. (3) The REE section concludes the sandstones formed in 'relatively deep seawater' (p. 19), at odds with the fluvial-lacustrine facies described (p. 4). (4) Abstract point (3) and Conclusion (3) list different source ranges and directions (§0 ¶1 vs p. 24). (5) The direction of the inferred tectonic trend versus the ratio trends is stated inconsistently (p. 16, 19). (6) The Dickinson/Crook check covers only the Lower Jurassic (Fig. 15). Sub-claims: the provenance directions (p. 10, 13) and the source-range assignments (p. 13-15) rest on 5-16 samples per epoch plus cited data, and are best_explanation at most. No uncertainties or sample-number limits are reported for any diagram assignment. Reading heavy-mineral data from other studies (Table 10) is inferred to be pooling rather than an independent check. The paper does not explicitly test its results against the open questions it raises (Bogda uplift timing; the Zhou et al. 2019 verification); my inference is that the questions remain unanswered. The paper sets no result explicitly against published work, so disagreements is empty.

alternatives_considered.chosen: McLennan (1993) correction for carbonate-hosted CaO in CIA (molar CaO:Na2O 1:1 in silicate fraction)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: not named; other CaO* corrections implied by citations to Nesbitt et al. 1982, Fedo et al. 1995, Feng et al. 2003
